title: Prove scope membership and unify aggregate closure with per-clause evaluation
description:
Decomposed out of eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1 (PR #475) 2026-07-27, user-approved, under the churn stop rule.

TWO DEFECTS, one cause: aggregate closure and per-clause evaluation are two evaluation paths that do not share a contract, and the scope they run over cannot prove what it claims.

SCOPE:
  * a branded scope must PROVE authoritative membership and record ownership, not merely carry a brand. An applicable scope with empty or selectively omitted membership must not return a false-green empty closure, and a clause from another record must not satisfy this scope.
  * aggregate closure must evaluate THE SAME CONTRACT as individual clauses — today it drops resolver context and additive requirements, so a clause can pass closure under weaker rules than it would face individually.

DEPENDENCY: needs the registry authority bead, since a scope cannot prove membership against an authority that cannot itself be proven.

PR #475 retains per-clause evaluation; this bead owns the aggregate path.
acceptance_criteria:
• A scope proves authoritative membership and exact family+record ownership; omitted membership and foreign-record clauses are rejected with tests.
• Aggregate closure evaluates the same contract as per-clause evaluation, including resolver context and additive requirements.
• A clause cannot pass closure under weaker rules than individual evaluation applies.
